subject: Animation
title: Scale and Camera: Making Villains Feel Huge
description: A 60-second lesson on Scale and Camera: Making Villains Feel Huge.

hook.text: Animated villains are often shot from low angles, making them tower over the audience and the hero.

buildup.text: Ursula grows to fill the entire ocean. Jafar becomes a giant snake. Maleficent becomes a dragon. Scale equals power.

discovery.text: Low camera angles trigger a primal response — anything above you feels threatening because it could fall on you.

twist.text: Some great villains are tiny. Ratatouille's Anton Ego is thin and small but is shot to look enormous and looming.

climax.text: Camera angle and scale are tools that animators use to make villains feel powerful regardless of their actual size.

punchline.text: In animation, the camera decides who is big and who is small.

quiz.question: How do animators use camera angles to make villains feel threatening?
options: They always draw villains physically larger than heroes
Low camera angles make villains tower over the viewer, triggering a primal sense of threat from above
Villains are always placed in the center of the frame
